headline: Advait Energy Transitions: Substantial Acquisition Disclosure Under SEBI Regulation 29(2)
sum: Advait Energy Transitions filed a SEBI Regulation 29(2) substantial acquisition disclosure with NSE, signalling a material change in shareholding that crossed regulatory thresholds; specific acquirer, share quantity, price, and acquisition method remain disclosed only in the full regulatory filing.
implication: This is a pure disclosure filing under takeover regulations rather than a completed M&A transaction—the precedent is the triggering of mandatory open-market or negotiated acquisition reporting once shareholding thresholds are crossed, and any parties reviewing this company should pull the full ST-1 form to assess insider risk, related-party concerns, and strategic intent.
detail: Advait Energy Transitions Limited filed a substantial acquisition disclosure under SEBI (SAST) Regulations 2011 Regulation 29(2) with the NSE on 18 June 2026. This disclosure indicates that an acquirer's shareholding has crossed one of the prescribed regulatory thresholds (commonly 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%, 90%, or 95%), triggering mandatory disclosure. The company is in the energy transition sector. The specific identity of the acquirer, the exact shareholding threshold crossed, the number of shares acquired, the acquisition price, and the method (open market, negotiated, or preferential) are all contained in the full disclosure document (typically Form ST-1 or a cover letter) filed with the NSE and require direct access to that filing to verify.
